description: This is a partial registry of established planning pins, not a complete inventory of every external normative dependency the floor drafts carry. Every entry carries a "kind" (git, datatracker, or standard) with kind-appropriate required fields: git needs repo, commit (full 40-hex), path, and sha256; datatracker needs doc, rev, url, and sha256; standard needs publisher and edition, with sha256 optional (paywalled standards carry no fetchable canonical file to hash, disclosed in the entry's note). Every entry also carries reference_keys: the exact citation key(s) as they appear in the drafts' kramdown front matter, which is how a bundle checker maps a document's cited references back to this registry. As of Ship 3, every entry in this registry is established; none is pending. Live-source verification (object type, path at commit or revision, content digest) against each entry's actual repository, datatracker revision, or published standard happens once, by hand, when a pin is established; it is disclosed per entry in that entry's note. A bundle manifest (notes/bundle-manifest.*.json) copies established entries here verbatim into its external_pins, and scripts/check-bundle-manifest.mjs enforces, on every run, that each copy is identical to its registry entry and that the build REJECTS if any registry entry a bundle consumes has status "pending". The bundle checker also derives the required external-pin set mechanically, on every run, by parsing each bundle document's normative front matter at its pinned commit and mapping the resulting citation keys through reference_keys; it rejects the build on any pin the derived set requires and the bundle omits, and on any pin the bundle carries that the derived set does not require. Completeness of this registry against the selected profiles' normative front matter is therefore enforced mechanically on every run, not checked by hand at Ship 3.

The citing draft's front matter carries no seriesinfo override on this reference (a bare `I-D.draft-ietf-oauth-status-list:` entry), so no revision is pinned in the draft text itself; this registry therefore pins the latest datatracker revision as of establishment (-21, confirmed via the datatracker document API, id 121268), which coincides with the implemented revision src/SPEC_VERSIONS.md already records for shipped code. pins.edition: ISO 4217:2015, Codes for the representation of currencies and funds
pins.note: draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission cites ISO4217 as a normative reference with front-matter seriesinfo `ISO: "4217:2015"`; this entry pins that same edition. No sha256: ISO 4217:2015 is a paywalled standard with no freely republishable canonical file, so there is no text this registry can legally fetch and hash; the publisher and edition identifier are the pin, and this note is the disclosed reason sha256 is absent. scripts/check-external-pins.mjs accepts a null sha256 only for kind "standard"; git and datatracker entries must always carry one.

pins.ref: GitHub tag 2026-07-28 (modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol), established at the #533 adoption review (2026-08-24)
pins.note: draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission cites MCP (Model Context Protocol: Authorization) as a normative reference for its tool-modeling section; this entry refreshes the family's pin from the retired 2025-11-25 legacy-handshake track (issue #533, split from #290) to the 2026-07-28 release. The `2026-07-28` tag is a lightweight tag confirmed via the git refs API to point directly at commit 5f5440bb26a62e2cf3440b92da5a667efa03b267 (the commit the tag resolves to: merge of PR #3158, 2026-07-28, the last merge before tagging). Located at docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx (confirmed via the repository contents API: blob sha b41b14e23eeecef953025d90d565d4ed18137dbc, size 25678 bytes, matching the fetched raw file this sha256 is computed over); the draft's own front-matter target already named this exact page and revision, so only this registry entry was missing. Adoption review disclosure: the 2026-07-28 diff's two deltas named at ruling (the statelessness redesign and the removed initialize/notifications/initialized handshake, both SEP-2575) were checked against this draft's claim that authorizing a tool's name as an action 'lines up with MCP filtering its tool list by the caller's granted authority'. The claim survives on direct textual confirmation, not inference: docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx (same commit) states the `tools/list` result set 'MUST NOT vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection' but 'MAY vary by the authorization presented on the request ... since credentials are per-request input, not connection state' (eliding the spec's own mid-sentence example, which names the same caller-scoped filtering this note describes); the CacheableResult `cacheScope: "private"` value (minor change, SEP-2549) corroborates this, since a private cache scope on a list result is only meaningful if list content can be caller-specific. Separately, formal Scope-Filtered Tool Discovery (SEP-1881) was never adopted into the spec at either revision (closed 2026-06-24 as a procedural casualty of the SEP-to-PR migration, not rejected on the merits); the tools.mdx text above is the spec's own affirmative statement of the same behavior, informal-SEP history aside. No prose changed.

pins.ref: GitHub tag 2026-07-28 (modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol), established at the #533 adoption review (2026-08-24)
pins.note: draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server cites MCP-META (Model Context Protocol: Base Protocol) as a normative reference for the MCP Carriage section's `_meta` namespacing rule; this entry refreshes the family's pin from the retired 2025-11-25 legacy-handshake track (issue #533, split from #290) to the 2026-07-28 release, the same tag and commit as the MCP entry above (5f5440bb26a62e2cf3440b92da5a667efa03b267), a different file within it. Located at docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx (confirmed via the repository contents API: blob sha dfe11ecc1443b7dec051b1b1b9a93982b735c647, size 25134 bytes, matching the fetched raw file this sha256 is computed over). The citing draft's own front-matter target and date were bumped from 2025-11-25 to 2026-07-28 in the same change that established this entry. Adoption review disclosure: the section's load-bearing claim is that `com.karlmcguinness.mission/reference` is a reverse-DNS-prefixed key outside MCP's own reserved `_meta` namespace. The 2026-07-28 revision states this rule more precisely than before (a prefix is MCP-reserved only when its second label is `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcp`), and the family's key's second label (`karlmcguinness`) is not reserved under that rule, so the claim holds, now on more explicit textual footing. The statelessness delta (SEP-2575) adds required per-request `_meta` fields but does not touch the reserved-prefix rule this section relies on, and it reinforces the section's own per-request, never-session-state, carriage rule. The section separately reads 'absent negotiated or configured propagation support the call MUST be refused': the removed initialize/notifications/initialized handshake was one way capability negotiation used to happen, but the sentence never named that mechanism, and per-request `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`, the `extensions` field, and `server/discover` are all still 'negotiated ... support' under the ordinary meaning of the word; this was a deliberate read, not an oversight, and the sentence is left as written. No prose changed beyond the pin refresh.
